items.reason: Detail status uses the same opener and entries over its own container.
Detail y opens the container’s Copy menu without copying.
Detail m opens the container’s Mute menu.
Both levels dispatch I through the shared container shortcut handler.
Peek handling removes both direct copy bindings.
Neither detail list retains a direct p binding.
Existing item and artifact r-menu handling remains intact.
Shared status refusal routes to the detail’s flash.
Copy and mute refusals use shared wording and the detail’s flash.
Container menus occupy the detail Frame’s reserved Block.
Detail menus reuse existing navigation and verb dispatch.
Menu Escape clears the menu without dismissing the detail.
Detail openers bypass Selection and target one container.
Slash starts detail search; Enter commits and restores navigation.
Shared filtering ANDs case-insensitive substring terms across id, title and type.
Item search fields exclude status.
Artifact filtering uses the same grammar over name and type.
Escape restores the previously applied term.
Search starts empty, and committing an empty query restores all rows.
Typing routes printable keys into TextField rather than detail actions.
Refresh reapplies the query, and the header displays the committed term.
Empty search results name the term and explain how to clear it.
Artifact availability uses the unfiltered collection, preserving v.
Detail search state is independently owned and disappears with the detail.
Detail hints advertise the requested menus and search; peek hints remove flat copies.
Typing hints name only apply, cancel and help.
Contextual help includes menus, applicable I, search and conditional clearing.
Menu help adapts to detail context, and detail typing has dedicated help.

scores.rationale: Shared dispatch and filtering keep complexity controlled, with focused regression tests; some asynchronous container feedback still targets the hidden row-list surface.
